1949, September 2
The following is the faithful transcription of the typewritten original by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, O.F.M. Cap.
ST. FELIX FRIARY
9/2/49 ROUTE 8 Blessed be God in all and each of His designs.
HUNTINGTON, INDIANA
God bless you Miss Benecki, - you and yours;
and many thanks for your kind remembrance and and treat which latter, came in very handy for several guests who came last evening this a.m. twenty-six novices took simple vows at the solemn services .... Deo gratias.
However, I'll now have to rather change my tone and scold you for your un- wonted soliditude about health or doctor or anything else. ... You surely want to get to Heaven. But how? Without dying? ... Ahl but in so vigerously pro- testing against this or that trouble, you as much as tell Divine Providence (in a way at least) "if I can't have at least something of a choice .... it will be all off; I can't make the grade." ...
Just think, dear Soul. What would have become of humanity if in the Gar- den of Gethsesemini, Jesus had insisted on His own will: "Heavenly Father its too much! ... " instead of: ... Not what I will, but what Thou willst ... ". 01 Where is our faith? Where are our proofs of love of Jesus, if suffering for the sake of the loved One be a proof of love? ? ? ! ! !
We ought to keep in mind as much as our poor frailities permit, especially in times of pains and sorrow; the thought of ETERNITY and the contrast of it with momentary passing for each one of us and the vanity of temperal phenomina - be they pleasant or painful to nature. We ought to thank God for both - for each and all these experiences. .
Even Jesus could not have accepted that decision of His heavenly Father, according to His human nature and with the divine nature, viz, without the grace of the Father. Hence, His continual communion with the Father and the Holy Spirit. Hence too our obligation to imitate Him, at least try at a distance.
To get to Heaven! Think of it. 0! Is it not infinitely more than we can pay for it whatever way we consider it? When it was so great in the estimation of the Son of God Jesus and His for each one of us that He died for each of us! Then, what matter if I die with cancer or TB or a martyr some other way - To- day, tomorow or fifty years ahead? Shame on you as well as on myself. Stupid we are every one of, in our feat of following Jesus to Heaven even if the cross and death the way. P.S. Shake off that worry-half the victory over any trouble.
Praised be Jesus Christ
.... Fr. Solanus, O.F.M. Cap.
